text: {"score":3,"justification":"The numbers match the card and the leaning (inconclusive) is cautious, with a sensible next step of requesting more charts. But the narrative contradicts the card in places, and the recommendation to target 99214s and 99215s on 2-3 condition patients is only partly supported. An investigator would have to recheck some of the analysis.","problems":["The headline and body say the excess sits in moderately complex (2-3 condition) patients, but those rows differ from the all-provider rate by only 0.128 vs 0.052 and 0.128 vs 0.08. The 4 and 5+ condition rows also run well above the all-provider rate, so the excess is broader than described.","The claim that at 0-1 conditions the provider 'tracks peers' is loosely supported: 0.018 vs 0.028 and 0.044 vs 0.041. It is acceptable but is stated with more confidence than the numbers allow.","The text says C0054446 as a low-MDM 99214, but the card lists C0054446 as 99214 low; the 'e.g.' citation is fine, but C0053695 is a 99213 and is cited among the examples without being mentioned in the narrative.","The summary calls 3 of 7 documented 99214s low MDM 'well above the comparison rate' (0.429 vs 0.037), but with n=7 this is very thin. It does hedge with 'weak but notable'.","The statement 'especially given how heavily this provider bills 99214' is unsupported by any comparison on the card; 526 of 897 claims is 59% but no peer rate is given.","The mechanical examples include two low-complexity 99215s (C0053518, C0053531) that sit awkwardly beside a headline saying low-complexity visits are not the driver, so the cited claims do not support the narrative.","The next steps are generic and do not name specific claim IDs for record requests. The narrative mentions C0054144 and C0054435, but the next_steps list does not.","The reference to 0 of 8 notes lacking a lab line is presented as meaningful, but it is not tied to a concern. The summary also does not flag that the 3 documented 99215s are too few to support anything."]}
